gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-13 the cheapest station that can run the booth's 1,500 W blender is $399 (ALLPOWERS P1800, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, at iallpowers.com). None states that the BLUETTI AC180 ChatGPT quoted at $449 now costs $499 at BLUETTI US, the same as BLUETTI's 1,024 Wh Elite 100 V2, or that ChatGPT's budget pick, the AC70, is sold out at BLUETTI and has a 1,000 W inverter.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. portableenergylab.com names no model and gives no price or $/Wh, only size ranges (300–500 Wh, 700–1,000 Wh). Our own dealectric page still shows the AC180 at $449, dated 2026-11-03, which is now out of date. I also read Volt & Valley (result 8, not cited). It gives Amazon prices dated Nov 13 for the Elite 200 V2 ($898.99) and Anker C1000 Gen 2 ($529.99), but it has no AC180, P1800, S2000 Pro, Elite 100 V2 or DELTA 3 Classic price, no $/Wh, and no line on the AC70's stock or inverter. ChatGPT's plain chat priced the DELTA 3 Plus at Costco, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at Eco Solar Kits, and the AC70 at $359 without noting that the AC70 is sold out.
decides: The AC180 stays a sound pick, but the reason changes. At $499 it no longer undercuts anything. It costs the same as the Elite 100 V2 and gives 128 Wh more, at $0.43/Wh, the same rate as the Elite 200 V2 at $899. For a shopper focused on price, the ALLPOWERS P1800 at $399 ($0.39/Wh, LiFePO4, 1,800 W) now covers the same 0.7–1.0 kWh day with the blender, and the S2000 Pro at $549 gives 1,451.5 Wh for $0.38/Wh. The AC70 should drop out as a budget pick for this booth: its 1,000 W inverter can't take a 1,500 W blender, and every BLUETTI listing for it is out of stock. The page's AC180 price and date need updating.
